title: Ramadan: planning
hook: a plan for reading, prayer, charity and rest

segments.voice: Yesterday, Rajab and Sha'ban: sacred time first, then the month he fasted most outside Ramadan. Today, the door opens.

A sheet of paper taped to a fridge door, a few days before the new moon. Four words across the top: reading, prayer, charity, rest. A portion of the Qur'an a day. Which nights at the mosque. Who gets the zakat, and when. What time the alarm goes off for the meal before dawn, and what time the phone goes off at night. It doesn't look holy. It looks like a schedule. But some families do exactly this before Ramadan, because a month can slip past on good intentions alone.
screen: `A SHEET OF PAPER, FOUR WORDS.` → `IT LOOKS LIKE A SCHEDULE.` → `A MONTH CAN SLIP PAST.`

segments.voice: You met Ramadan on day six, and walked through its days in year one. Now, how to arrive on purpose. Begin with reading, because the Qur'an ties the month to the book. Surah al-Baqarah, in Pickthall's words: "The month of Ramadan in which was revealed the Qur'an, a guidance for mankind, and clear proofs of the guidance, and the Criterion." Ibn 'Abbas reports in al-Bukhari that Jibril would meet the Prophet, peace be upon him, every night of Ramadan and go over the Qur'an with him. So a reading plan follows the habit Ibn 'Abbas describes. Then charity, which the same report ties to the reading: the Prophet was the most generous of people, and most generous of all in Ramadan when Jibril met him, more generous, he says, than a wind sent out. Then prayer: in another hadith in al-Bukhari, whoever stands in prayer through Ramadan out of faith and hoping for reward is forgiven past sins. Then rest, the column people forget. The same verse says: "Allah desireth for you ease; He desireth not hardship for you." The month is meant to be hard enough to change you, not so hard it breaks you. In al-Bukhari, the Prophet tells people to eat the meal before dawn, because there's blessing in it. Sleep, food and water are part of the plan, not a failure of it. And look back at this week: the life cycle closed, then the year opened, the sacred months, Muharram, Ashura, Rabi' al-Awwal, Rajab and Sha'ban, all walking toward this one month.
screen: `READING: THE MONTH OF THE BOOK.` · `GIVING, LIKE A WIND SENT OUT.` · `REST: ALLAH DESIRETH FOR YOU EASE.` · `A WEEK WALKING TOWARD ONE MONTH.`

segments.voice: Picture the sheet of paper and its four words, and give each one a short line: a realistic amount of reading a day, one time of prayer you'll protect, one person or cause to give to, one thing you'll keep for rest. Keep each line short enough to actually do. If you won't fast, the same four words still work for any month you want to keep well.
Ramadan. The month of fasting, the month al-Baqarah says the Qur'an was revealed in, with room for reading, prayer, charity and rest. Today's word.
Your line: plan the month. A plan is how you arrive on purpose. Tomorrow, the family table.

howItsDone: Muslims fast from dawn to sunset in Ramadan, and some make a plan beforehand for reading the Qur'an, night prayer, charity and zakat, and enough sleep and food at the pre-dawn meal, drawing on Qur'an 2:185 and hadiths in al-Bukhari.

chat.says: Why would someone write out a plan for Ramadan? Isn't it just fasting?
options: It's more: reading, prayer and charity too, and rest, since Allah wants ease for you.
It's just fasting; the Qur'an says nothing else about the month at all.
Plans are for the strong; the harder you push, the better the month.
chat.meaning: The Qur'an ties Ramadan to its revelation, Ibn 'Abbas ties it to reading and generosity, and al-Baqarah says Allah desires ease, not hardship.
